FMC × Adobe · postinpremiere.com

Hero redesign — before and after

The event, copy, and Adobe interface capture are unchanged. What changed is how the hero presents them: type hierarchy, the live-training badge, a graded cinematic background, and a tighter benefits rail. Two candidate directions below — pick one.

Before — the live site today

Current hero

Ground-level rally car photo, one-line subtitle, small copy paragraph, three-item info band.

Option A · recommended for the site

Cinematic grade + Premiere panel

The background becomes the raw aerial footage, graded dark and cinematic — and the panel beside it is the real, untouched Adobe capture showing that same footage split-graded in Premiere's Color Mode. The page literally demonstrates what the training teaches.

  • "Live Online Training" becomes a cyan outlined badge above the headline — what-this-is reads first
  • Subtitle steps up to a two-line second deck, "Post-Production" on its own line
  • Date is the dominant fact below the copy; time + "On Zoom, Worldwide" sit in a small icon row
  • Premiere logo lives on the interface panel — where the software actually is
  • Panel sits in a charcoal slab, giving the capture weight against the image
  • Rail trimmed to the three distinct promises, replay first: 180-day replay, captions, dubbing on request
Option B · campaign / approval imagery

Car only, no panel

Same layout, full-bleed aerial with the car carving the frame. More atmospheric — but without the interface, the Premiere tile moves into the badge to keep the software present. Better suited to campaign imagery than the site hero, where the panel is the proof this is software training.

Option A variant

Same hero, four-item rail

Identical to Option A but the rail keeps "Join Live from Anywhere" as a fourth item.

Recommendation

Ship Option A. Option B is the stronger standalone image, but it could open any automotive campaign — Option A is the only version that proves this is Premiere training. The background image in both options is pending final asset approval from Adobe.
